transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… what brings me in is my body doesn’t feel like it’s fully listening to me. Like, for a while I was pacing around the apartment all night, making all these notes for this supper-club idea I had — I used to work service, so I know how the flow should go, table timing and all that — but I just couldn’t stop moving.

And now it’s kind of the opposite. I’m so slowed down lately that my sister says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on. It’s embarrassing, honestly. Like I’m stuck in myself.
Have you ever experienced a time when your mood was extremely high or you felt unusually energetic, maybe even reckless, for several days or longer?

Yeah… yeah, there was a stretch like that. It was after I got fired, which sounds like it should’ve knocked me down, but instead I felt, I don’t know, weirdly unstoppable. Like suddenly everything was possible and I had all these plans, and I felt excited in this intense way.

But then if anyone questioned me — like my sister saying maybe I should slow down, or asking if the plan made sense — I’d just snap. Like really blow up, like they were trying to wreck my whole life on purpose. I know that sounds dramatic, but in the moment it felt completely true.
How long did that stretch of feeling unusually energetic and excited last? Was it more than a week or less than that?

It was definitely more than a week. I mean… it started after I got fired from the restaurant, and it kind of just kept going. I’d say around four months, which sounds crazy when I say it out loud.

The restaurant thing was messy too, because I’d worked there long enough to know everybody’s habits, like who would disappear during side work and who’d steal the good sections—sorry, that’s not what you asked. But yeah, the energy and all that… about four months.
After that four-month period of high energy and excitement, did you experience a period where you felt very down, depressed, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yeah… after that, I went way down. Or, I mean, not right like a light switch, but the heavy, slowed-down part has been there for about three months now.

It’s weird because I’ll think about how fast everything felt before, and now even small stuff feels like it takes forever. Sorry, I’m kind of circling it — yes, it’s been months, not just a couple bad days.
Have you ever had other periods in your life when you felt extremely energetic, unusually confident, or needed less sleep for at least a few days?

I mean… the main one I keep thinking about is after I got fired. That was when I felt weirdly unstoppable, like I had all this confidence and excitement out of nowhere.

And it wasn’t just “good mood” stuff either — if anyone questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down, I’d blow up. Like my sister could say one thing about my plan not making sense, and I’d take it like she was trying to ruin my life. I’m sure there were probably little versions of that before, but that one is the clearest.
Have you had any other times in your life when you felt unusually energetic, confident, or required much less sleep — even if it was for just a few days?

Yeah, I mean… the big one is still after I got fired. That’s the one that sticks out the most.

I felt weirdly unstoppable, like excited and confident in a way that didn’t really feel normal for me. And then if somebody questioned me — like told me my plans didn’t make sense or I should slow down — I’d just snap at them. Like, not just annoyed, more like they were trying to ruin everything for me.

I know you’re asking if there were other times too… I’m trying to think, but that period is the clearest one.
Have you ever had times when your mood was noticeably more upbeat or energized than usual, even if it didn’t last very long?

Yeah… I think so. The one I keep coming back to is after I got fired. I know I’ve already mentioned that, sorry, but that’s when my mood was just way more… charged, I guess. Like I felt weirdly unstoppable and excited, like everything I was thinking made total sense.

And then, I don’t know, people would ask normal questions — my sister especially, because she worries — and I’d take it like they were attacking me or trying to ruin my whole plan. I’d blow up at them instead of just answering. It felt upbeat at first, but also really irritable if anyone got in my way.
Can you recall if there was ever a time when you had an unusually elevated or irritable mood that lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week?

Yeah… I think that firing period was probably like that. It wasn’t just an hour here or there — most days I woke up already feeling wired, like I was on some kind of mission.

I felt weirdly unstoppable and excited, like my plans were obviously right, and then if anyone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d just blow up. Like my sister would say something normal and I’d hear it as her trying to ruin my whole life.

Sorry, I know I keep circling back to that, but that’s the time that really fits.
Have you had three or more separate periods in your life where you felt unusually energetic, confident, or needed much less sleep than usual?

Three or more? I… honestly don’t know. I can’t really line them up like that.

I keep thinking about that one period after I got fired, because that’s the one everyone remembers and brings up, but three separate times… I’m not sure. My memory kind of gets messy with stuff like that. Like, I’ll think, “Was that another period, or was I just stressed, or working weird shifts?” because restaurant hours mess with your sleep anyway.

So I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. I can really only point to the one clearly.

Can you think of another time in your life, separate from the period after you got fired, when you felt unusually upbeat, irritable, or had so much energy that it was noticeably different from your usual self?

I’m trying to think, but I don’t have another clear one that I can point to and say, “Yeah, that was definitely like that.”

Like, there were busy stretches in college or at work where everything was chaotic and my schedule was all over the place, but that feels different, you know? Restaurant life is kind of already weird — late nights, people calling out, managers changing the schedule last minute — so it’s hard for me to separate what was me from what was just the situation.

So… no, not that I can really remember clearly. The firing thing is the one that stands out.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, and lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… the interest part, definitely. I mean, I don’t know if I’m tracking the days perfectly, but the stuff that usually keeps me steady just feels… flat.

Like cooking used to be my thing — I’d mess around with recipes, take photos of food, put music on, make a whole thing out of it. And pickup soccer, volunteering, all that stuff… I know I used to care about it, but now it’s like I can remember caring without actually feeling it.

It’s weird, because I’ll even look at my camera roll sometimes and think, “Oh, I was really into this,” and then I just don’t have anything in me about it.

Before this most recent time of feeling down and slowed down, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt depressed or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, and lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve had rough patches before, definitely, but whether it was two weeks straight like that… I don’t really know.

Sometimes I think back to school, because there were times I’d stop going out much, but then I also had classes and work and money stuff, and I’d get caught up in like, trying to fix my schedule or switching shifts. It all kind of blends together.

So I don’t want to say yes like I’m sure. Before this recent time, I can’t really point to a clear period that fits exactly what you’re asking.

Can you think of another time — separate from the period after you got fired — when you had a clear change in mood where you felt unusually high, irritable, or energized for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a few days in a row?

I mean… not really another time. The one after I got fired is the one I keep coming back to.

That was the time where I felt, like, weirdly unstoppable. Excited, almost like everything suddenly made sense and I had all these plans. And I know people say stuff like that when they’re just trying to bounce back, but this felt different.

And then if anybody questioned me — like told me to slow down or asked if I was sure — I’d just snap. Like, I’d take it as them trying to ruin my life or block me from doing what I needed to do. I got really irritated fast.

But separate from that? I can’t really think of another clear stretch like that.
Can you think of another time — not the one after you got fired — when you had several days in a row of feeling unusually energetic, confident, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Not really… I keep trying to scan back through, but I don’t have another clear example like that.

I mean, there were nights in college where I stayed up late, but that was more because everyone was up late, or I had work early, or I’d get pulled into some random thing with roommates — like one time we decided at 2 a.m. to reorganize the whole apartment, which sounds weird now, but it wasn’t like… several days of me being a totally different person.

So, no, not one I can point to. The firing thing is the one that stands out.
